jobs.title: Lead, People Case Management
jobs.description:
About Newmont

Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.

Your role

Reporting to the Director, People Business Partner and Labour Relations, Australia Asia Pacific, in the position of Lead, People Case Management , you will lead and oversee a People Case Management team across Newmont’s Africa Asia Pacific region to plan and execute internal investigations related to Tier 2 ‘Respect at Work’ cases including sexual misconduct, discrimination, harassment, bullying and intimidation.

Other key responsibilities

- Lead sensitive and complex workplace investigations including discrimination, sexual harassment, sexual misconduct and other ‘Respect at Work’ matters
- Assign and oversee investigations undertaken by others and provide expert guidance and quality assurance
- Prepare clear, objective and evidence-based investigation reports and maintain accurate, confidential case records
- Ensure investigations are fair, thorough and aligned with relevant legislative, regulatory and procedural requirements
- Present findings to management and provide expert input to support appropriate corrective and disciplinary outcomes
- Identify investigation trends and insights to inform training, policy, awareness and preventative initiatives
- Drive continuous improvement in investigation methodologies, case management, tools, reporting and dashboards.

What you will bring

- Tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Law, Business, Accounting or related
- Formal Certification in Workplace Investigations
- Certified Fraud Examiner, Certified Internal Auditor or equivalent
- Significant experience conducting complex and sensitive workplace investigations within a large, multinational organisation
- Strong knowledge of workplace investigation practices, procedural fairness and relevant legislative and regulatory requirements
- Experience in mining, construction, utilities and/or heavy industry
- Experience with eDiscovery and digital forensics
- Demonstrated capability in evidence gathering, interviewing, analysis and investigation report writing
- Sound judgement, discretion and stakeholder management skills
- Proficient skills in reporting tools and data analytics
- Proven team leadership across geographic locations with the ability to champion collaboration
- Full and unrestricted eligibility to work in Australia.

Your work environment

This permanent full-time position will be based out of Newmont Australia’s Brisbane or Perth capital city hub and will suit applicants currently living in Brisbane or Perth who have full and unrestricted eligibility to work in Australia.

At Newmont, our people are our strength, and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.

Applications close COB 26 October 2026.

jobs.title: Specialist People Business Partner
jobs.description:
About Newmont

Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.

Your role

Reporting to the Director People, the Specialist People Business Partner will provide site-based HR business partnering support across Newmont’s remote Tanami operations in the Northern Territory.

Working closely with operational and senior leadership teams you will provide practical, trusted advice across employee relations and the broader employee lifecycle.

As part of a small and collaborative People team you will also be required to operate confidently as the on-site People representative during roster rotations.

Key responsibilities

- Partner with operational and senior leaders to provide practical HR advice and support across employee relations, performance management, workforce matters and annual people processes
- Manage employee grievances, investigations and disciplinary matters in accordance with Newmont policies, Australian employment legislation and applicable workplace arrangements
- Partner with leaders to manage organisational change and transformation activities, provide coaching and guidance to build leadership capability, support employee transitions and embed sustainable change outcomes
- Work closely with Talent Acquisition and People Services to support workforce requirements, employee data integrity and effective delivery of People services on site
- Support the implementation of Newmont People initiatives including employee engagement, change management, diversity and inclusion and global HR standards
- Build strong relationships across the operation and promote Newmont’s Values and a positive, inclusive workplace culture.

Your skills and experience

- Tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline, with demonstrated HR generalist or business partnering experience in a site-based mining, resources or similarly complex operational environment
- Strong practical knowledge of Australian employment and employee relations legislation including the Fair Work framework, enterprise agreements, grievance management and disciplinary processes
- Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex people matters and confidently support operational and senior leadership teams within a large, remote mine operation
- Strong stakeholder management, communication and influencing skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office and SAP
- Ability to work a FIFO roster in a permanent site-based role with full and unrestricted Australian working rights.

Your work environment

Tanami is one of Australia’s most remote and significant underground gold mines, located deep in the Tanami Desert of the Northern Territory. As a fully fly-in, fly-out (FIFO) operation, Tanami flies around 1,800 employees and contractors to site via its own airstrip, with teams working on a rotational camp roster. The mine was originally an open-pit operation but has evolved into a world-class underground asset with extensive modern infrastructure. A major expansion (Tanami Expansion 2) is underway – including a 1.5-kilometre-deep hoisting shaft – to extend Tanami’s life beyond 2040 and increase production efficiency. The remote location fosters a close-knit team spirit, where safety and mutual respect are paramount. Tanami’s workforce is proud to work in partnership with the local Warlpiri people on whose land we operate, ensuring that our presence contributes positively to communities. Working at Tanami means tackling unique technical challenges in a supportive environment, with a strong focus on Always Safe, responsible operations and improving daily to secure this mine’s long-term future.

This Tanami site-based position will work on a fly in fly out roster of 8 days on site, 6 days off from point of hire Perth, Brisbane, Alice Springs or Darwin.

At Newmont, our people are our strength, and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.

Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: it.sec@newmont.com.

Applications close COB Friday 16 October 2026.

jobs.title: Specialist Organizational Development
jobs.description:
Workplace Type:  Hybrid
Posting End Date:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our global headquarters in Denver, Colorado is a hub of innovation and collaboration. Here, multi-disciplinary teams chart strategy and provide technical, financial and operational leadership to support Newmont’s mines worldwide. Denver Hub’s professionals work closely with colleagues across all our regions, tackling projects that influence the entire business. The atmosphere is professional yet people-centered – we celebrate innovation and constantly seek better ways of working. Employees enjoy a modern workspace and the perks of a city famous for its outdoor lifestyle and vibrant economy.
Your Contribution

To support organizational health by delivering and improving Organizational Development systems, governance and assurance processes that strengthen design integrity and organizational effectiveness across Newmont.

As a part of our team, you will

- Maintain and continuously improve Organizational Development systems, governance processes, Ways of Working and supporting tools in alignment with enterprise standards.
- Support stewardship of the approved organizational design by maintaining its authorized representation and ensuring design decisions are appropriately documented.
- Support the development, application and continuous improvement of organization design standards, structural principles, role relationships, decision criteria and conformance requirements.
- Perform periodic, risk-based organizational design assurance reviews to assess material alignment with the approved design and evaluate whether surrounding governance and operational controls are working as intended.
- Analyze structural health indicators and enterprise patterns, including layers, spans, organizational capacity, cost and structural drift, to identify material risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Identify systemic patterns and distinguish isolated discrepancies from recurring breakdowns in processes, capabilities, workflows, governance or control design.
- Prepare governance reporting, structural health insights, assurance findings and management information to support decision-making, enterprise risk escalation and Organizational Development priorities.
- Support the governance and sustainment of the Role Profile Library, including intake, quality review, role profile reconciliation, role architecture alignment, version control and ongoing maintenance.
- Provide guidance to People Business Partners and other People stakeholders on the application of Organizational Development systems, standards, governance processes and design assurance requirements.
- Coordinate the implementation and sustainment of Organizational Development programs, tools and Ways of Working, including process documentation, guidance materials, capability support, adoption monitoring and continuous improvement.

Prerequisites for your success in this role

- Bachelor’s degree in organizational psychology, organizational development, business administration, social sciences, or related field.
- Advanced understanding of organizational design principles and organizational effectiveness concepts.
- Understanding of change management principles and frameworks, awareness of how to manage and support organizational change.
- Understanding of organizational governance, assurance and Health of Discipline concepts.
- Understanding of workforce planning, organizational analytics and role architecture.
- Knowledge of organizational design technologies, including Orgvue and related People platforms.
- Understanding of Role Profile Library governance, role architecture and organizational structure management practices.
- Advanced proficiency in Orgvue and organizational design data analysis.
- Advanced facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Advanced written and verbal communications skills.
- Competent capability in workforce analytics, reporting and dashboard development.
- Competent capability in organizational assurance and governance processes.
- Competent understanding of role architecture, role profiling and organizational data structures.
- Competent capability in identifying trends, risks and improvement opportunities through data analysis.

Your work environment

This role operates within the Organization Development organization and partners closely with People Business Partners, Total Rewards, Talent Management, People Systems & Services, Workforce Planning and Business Planning as well as external consultants and advisors, industry associations and professional networks and technology platform providers.

Work Environment, Pay & Benefits:

This position is based in our Denver, CO corporate headquarters, with flexibility for hybrid work. The base salary range is 106,200- 141,600 (reflecting  market rates and your qualifications). The final base pay offer will be based on individual factors such as your experience, and skills – we do not ask for or use your prior pay in setting your compensation. You will also be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on company and personal performance. Newmont provides a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision insurance, health savings/reimbursement accounts, 401(k), pension, paid time off, and family leave.
Applying
When you apply, feel free to leave out age-related details like your birth date, graduation years or dates of attendance at educational institutions – it will not affect your application in any way.
Newmont and its affiliates are equal employment opportunity employers.  All qualified applicants for employment will be considered without regard to individual’s race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, religion, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. If you would like to request an accommodation in the application process due to a disability, please let your recruiter know. Newmont offers reasonable accommodations to candidates with disabilities.
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. jobs.title: Director, Global Treasury Operations
jobs.description:
Job Location: Corporate Headquarters
Workplace Type:  Hybrid
Recruiter Name: Mary Soiza
Job Grade: Level 3
Posting End Date:

Your contribution

Lead a team of treasury professionals responsible for cash management, banking infrastructure, liquidity management, forecasting, treasury systems, and governance activities. This role ensures the efficient management of cash, bank accounts, payments, investments, treasury controls, and banking relationships while driving process standardization, automation, and continuous improvement across a global operating environment.

As a part of our team, you will

- Lead global cash positioning, forecasting, and funding activities.
- Support working capital initiatives by executing the short-term cash forecasting process
- Drive opportunities to improve effectiveness and efficiency of assigned treasury process through automation and process simplification
- Lead the management and control of global bank accounts, authorized signers and KYC
- Oversee and ensure compliance with global treasury policies and serve as Treasury function SOX Champion
- Drive banking strategy and structure, evaluate new products and services, and negotiate bank fees
- Form relationships with our banking partners and key business partners such as accounting, legal, IT, and tax
- Lead, maintain, implement treasury management systems and tools
- Recommend foreign exchange strategies to reduce fx loss on transactions and cash
- Explain the purpose of the work of your team and how it adds value to the business.
- Encourage your team members to identify critical issues which will affect the work.
- Listen when issues are raised.
- Allocate work to your team to contribute to achieving the team goals.
- Review how team members are performing with their work.
- Recognize and reward good work, including through feedback and coaching.
- Work with your manager to build and develop your team, including recruiting and removing team members.
- Work with your manager to help develop the people on your team.
- Review the decisions of managers on your team and course correct when needed.
- Design roles for team members who work for the managers on your team.
- Foster a climate that is inclusive where team members feel safe to contribute and collaborate, receive feedback and coaching.

Prerequisites for success in this role

- MBA or equivalent degree
- Treasury management system implementation and optimization experience
- ERP solutions
- Knowledge of IFRS and/or U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Procedures (GAAP)
- Costing and budgeting concepts and techniques
- Global banking and banking regulations
- Understanding of capital markets
- Knowledge of Bloomberg
- Knowledge of banking systems

Your work environment

This role operates within the Treasury organization where you'll lead critical treasury initiatives, partner with teams across the business, and drive meaningful impact through process improvement and innovation. You'll lead and develop a high-performing team while fostering a collaborative, inclusive culture focused on continuous improvement and business success.

We understand no candidate will meet every single desired qualification. If your experience looks a little different from what we’ve identified and you think you can bring value to the role, we’d love to learn more about you!

The salary range offered for this role is USD $168,800.00-$241,200.00. The salary range is tied to the Colorado market for jobs performed in Colorado. The salary offer to the successful candidate will be based on job-related education, training, and/or experience.  The salary offer will not be based on a candidate’s salary history at other jobs, and by law, Newmont will not seek information about salary history, and candidates should not share such information with Newmont.

This role will be eligible for participation in a discretionary annual bonus program, pursuant to which an employee may be awarded a percentage of their salary based on the company’s performance and their own individual performance. This role also will be eligible for participation in a discretionary long-term incentive program, pursuant to which an employee may receive awards based on their level and individual performance.

Newmont offers a competitive and inclusive benefits package to support physical, mental, financial and emotional wellbeing. This role will be eligible for the following benefits:  Medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision insurance; flexible spending accounts; health savings accounts; life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance; short and long-term disability; defined benefit pension; 401(k) program with company match; financial planning; employee assistance program (EAP); wellbeing reimbursement program; adoption assistance; tuition reimbursement; paid holidays and paid time off; paid family leave; matching gifts; and discounts on home, auto and pet insurance.  All bonuses and benefits are subject to the applicable eligibility and program/plan terms and may be modified or terminated at Newmont’s sole discretion.

When submitting your resume or CV or any other application materials (including school transcripts, proof of graduation, etc.) to Newmont, it's important to focus on your relevant skills, experience, and qualifications to show how well you fit the role. Pursuant to Colorado law, you may choose to remove or redact any age-identifying information (for example, age, date of birth, dates of school attendance, dates of school graduation, etc.).  You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.  Newmont is an equal employment opportunity employer, and does not make hiring decisions based on age or any other protected characteristics (e.g., gender, sexual orientation, disability, race, national origin, religion).

Please note that if you are offered a position, the company may need to verify your date of birth for preemployment screening purposes including background check and prohibited party screening.  But age-related information is not required for the application process.

jobs.title: GDC Sourcing Analyst
jobs.description:
At Newmont, people create the value in the metals we mine and are ambassadors in the communities where they live and work. As a team, we foster an environment in support of our people vision, where everyone belongs, thrives and is valued. We have built a diverse and inclusive workplace where our people can bring their differences to support delivering  results together. Newmont’s Service Enablement Group (SEG) is a new internal Newmont function that aims to improve processes and service delivery for the organization. It is comprised of two parts: A Process Excellence team and a future-state service delivery model who design will be informed by the work of the Process Excellence team.
Join us and unearth your potential in a global company that is at the forefront of shaping the future of the mining industry.
Your Impact

As an Analyst, Sourcing Services, you will help Newmont make informed supplier decisions by delivering accurate, timely, and high-quality sourcing data. Your work will support cost efficiency, sustainability, and performance improvements across our global supply chain.

As Part of Our Team, You Will

- Prepare supplier information to guide choices, assess risks, and manage relationships.
- Reconcile and report supplier performance on cost, quality, reliability, sustainability, and delivery speed.
- Support process improvements, new tools, and systems to streamline workflows.
- Assist in auditing and data quality initiatives.
- Collaborate with colleagues across disciplines and global locations to achieve sourcing goals.

Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role

- Technical qualifications or degree in Supply Chain, Finance, Engineering, or Business Administration.
- 2–4 years’ experience in procurement, sourcing, or supply chain (shared services preferred).
- Proficiency in ERP/SAP (Ariba experience highly desirable) and Microsoft Office, especially Excel.
- Knowledge of P2P processes, supplier performance metrics, and regulatory compliance in US/global markets.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and collaboration skills.

Your Work Environment

- You will be part of Newmont’s Global Delivery Center (GDC) in Costa Rica, working within the Corporate function. The role is people-focused and involves cross-functional collaboration with global stakeholders across People, Finance, IT, and Supply Chain teams.
- While the position is intended to be hybrid, as we establish our foundation, we will begin on-site to foster strong relationships, align our strategies, and ensure a solid framework for long-term success.
- This role is for the day shift schedule.
- Compensation will be aligned with the local Costa Rican market and paid in Costa Rican colones (CRC).

Why Join Newmont

- Work with one of the world’s leading gold producers committed to safety, inclusion, and sustainability.
- Gain valuable experience in global procurement and process improvement.
- Competitive pay, benefits, and opportunities for growth and development.

We understand no candidate will meet every single desired qualification. If your experience looks a little different from what we’ve identified and you think you can bring value to the role, we’d love to learn more about you! Our business success comes from the accomplishments and well-being of our employees and contractors. Our goal is to build a workplace culture that fosters leaders and allows every person to thrive, contribute, and grow. We are committed to selecting and developing our employees, and to establishing a work environment where everyone can take an active part in reaching our strategic goals while feeling a sense of pride in working at Newmont.
Newmont seeks to recruit, hire, place and promote qualified applicants, meaning applicants who meet the minimum requirements of the position, without regard to personal characteristics such as gender, race, nationality, ethnic, social and indigenous origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
